name: Bodegas AAlto Ribera del Duero AAlto 2015
text:
## Bodegas AAlto Ribera del Duero AAlto 2015

**The story.** AAlto was founded by Mariano García and Javier Zaccagnini in the [Ribera del Duero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribera_del_Duero) of Castile, to make deep, complex reds from the region's old vines ([Noble Sélection, the Quebec agent](https://nobleselection.kork.ca/en/our-wineries/aalto/ribera-del-duero/2015)). García's pedigree is the reason the wine was famous from its first vintages: he was the winemaker at [Vega Sicilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Sicilia), Spain's most celebrated estate, from 1968 to 1996, the main disciple of Jesús Anadón, before leaving to make his own wines ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Sicilia)).

**The neighbour that set the bar.** Vega Sicilia was founded in 1864 by Eloy Lecanda y Chaves, who brought Bordeaux vines home to Castile; [Hugh Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Johnson_%28wine_writer%29) famously called it "the Latour; but Latour of a vintage that has raisined the grapes and fried the picking crews", a nod to the Ribera's hot summers ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Sicilia)). The name has nothing to do with Sicily: "vega" is the green riverbank of the Duero, and "Sicilia" is Saint Cecilia, patron saint of musicians ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Sicilia)).

**The wine.** AAlto is 100% [Tempranillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempranillo) (Tinto Fino, as it is called locally), at 14.5% alcohol ([Noble Sélection](https://nobleselection.kork.ca/en/our-wineries/aalto/ribera-del-duero/2015)). It is the estate's main wine; the rarer AAlto PS stands for "Pagos Seleccionados", selected plots. For recent vintages the Wine Advocate reports 18 months in French and American oak and around 330,000 bottles, a big production for a wine of this standing ([Noble Sélection, 2020 review](https://nobleselection.kork.ca/en/our-wineries/aalto/ribera-del-duero/2015)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Rioja and Ribera del Duero vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/rioja-and-ribera-del-duero) says Ribera was hot and dry in 2015: old vines did well while younger ones struggled, the crop was down by up to a third on 2014, and the wines show very high flavour ripeness with soft tannins and high alcohol, turning out "much better than was perhaps expected".

**What the critics say for 2015.** I couldn't read a 2015 review from a source I can open (the reviews I found sit on sites that block me), so I've left critics' scores out rather than guess.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.7** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old, and your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2030. So it is in its prime: dark plum and blackberry, with the oak now folded into cocoa, tobacco and spice. Decant an hour ahead and serve at 16 to 18°C.

**Food.** Castile's classic is [lechazo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lechazo), milk-fed lamb roasted in a wood oven; otherwise roast lamb, a grilled ribeye, or aged [Manchego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchego).

**Value and where to buy.** BSW Liquor has the AAlto 2022 at $121 and the AAlto PS at $250; ZYN has the AAlto 2023 at $117 and the PS from $214.

**Curious details**
- **A record bottle.** In 2022 a vertical of 36 vintages of Vega Sicilia's Único, García's old wine, sold at a Swiss auction for €111,477 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Sicilia)).
- **Patience as a style.** Vega Sicilia has held wines back for decades: in 1991 it released the 1968 and the 1982 together ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Sicilia)).

Sources:
